**Top of mind:** Nvidia is in talks to lead/join a round valuing Mercor at $20B — double its October mark — after paying Mercor directly for expert data to train its open-source Nemotron models. The signal for vendors: chipmakers and infra players are now buying human-expert data on their own account, not just the frontier labs, and the marginal dollar is moving from bulk annotation toward verified agentic environments and expert trajectories. Micro1 quietly crossing a $500M gross run rate in eight months confirms the demand is broad, not concentrated in the top three.

## Competitor moves

- **Nvidia in talks to back Mercor at a $20B valuation, doubling October's mark.** General Catalyst is discussing leading the round; Nvidia paid Mercor millions last quarter to source specialist data for Nemotron, so this is a customer converting into an investor — a pattern worth watching for anyone pitching chip and infra vendors as buyers rather than just labs. [The Information](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/nvidia-discusses-funding-ai-data-supplier-mercor-20-billion-valuation), [Tech Startups](https://techstartups.com/2026/08/19/nvidia-in-talks-to-invest-in-ai-data-startup-mercor-at-20-billion-valuation/), [PYMNTS](https://www.pymnts.com/news/investment-tracker/2026/nvidia-weighs-investment-in-round-valuing-mercor-at-20-billion/)
- **Micro1 hits a $500M gross annual run rate, up from $100M in eight months.** Net is reportedly $150–200M after contractor pass-through (60–70% retention), but off-the-shelf datasets resold to multiple buyers carry 80–90% gross margin — a reminder that the reusable-dataset line, not bespoke labeling, is where the margin actually lives. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/20/ai-data-startup-micro1-reaches-500m-gross-run-rate-amid-ai-training-boom/), [Dealroom](https://dealroom.co/news/146247-micro1-hits-500m-gross-run-rate-as-ai-data-demand-surges/)
- **Mercor booked $614M in H1 2026 revenue, up ~70% YoY, but 91% came from foundation-model customers.** That concentration is the sector's shared fragility: a single lab re-insourcing or switching vendors moves the P&L materially, which is the argument for enterprise and government diversification. [The Information](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/handshake-mercor-revenue-surges-demand-human-contractors-train-ai)

## New projects & opportunities

- **Greenko's AM Intelligence places a binding ~9,000-unit Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 order for a Hyderabad cluster, ~$8B capex.** Targeting 200MW near-term scaling toward 1GW of compute-as-a-service across India, the US, Finland and Malaysia, with ~450 exaFLOPS of NVFP4 inference planned in Hyderabad — India-based compute at this scale creates local demand for evaluation, red-teaming and Indic-language data close to the metal. [Taipei Times](https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/biz/archives/2026/08/26/2003863126)
- **OpenAI begins showing ads on ChatGPT Free and Go tiers in India, starting with 50 brands via WPP and Omnicom.** India is now 100M+ weekly ChatGPT users; ad-safety classification, brand-suitability labeling and Indic-language quality evaluation are all near-term RFP shapes that follow a launch like this. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/27/openai-to-start-showing-ads-on-chatgpts-free-and-go-tiers-in-india/), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/28/openai-strategy-india-anthropic-ipo.html)
- **Skild AI ships S1, a robotics foundation model that executes 10-minute tasks from a single human video with no fine-tuning.** Reported 66% success on unseen tasks vs 9% for language-prompted VLAs at the same 100k-hour training scale — the scale figure is the tell: human demonstration video collection remains a volume business, and India-based teleop and demo capture is a credible offer. [Skild AI](https://www.skild.ai/blogs/s1)
- **General Intuition raises at a $6B pre-money, nearly triple its mark from eight weeks ago, to train world models on gameplay video.** Valor, Point72 Ventures and Seven Seven Six are in; the money is earmarked for pushing into robotic embodiments — another buyer for licensed video corpora and annotated interaction trajectories. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/24/valor-point72-back-general-intuition-at-6b-valuation-as-ai-startup-pushes-into-robotics/)

## Frontier lab movements

- **Anthropic tells IPO investors it expects to match or top SpaceX's record IPO size, pitching a $30T market opportunity.** It filed a confidential S-1 on 1 June; a listing at reported $2T scale would put unprecedented disclosure pressure on training-data sourcing and contractor practices across its whole supply chain — expect procurement diligence to tighten. [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-20/anthropic-expects-to-match-spacex-s-record-ipo-size-or-top-it), [Quartz](https://qz.com/anthropic-ipo-investors-30-trillion-market-opportunity-082526), [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/news/confidential-draft-s1-sec)
- **SemiAnalysis details OpenAI's Jalapeño inference chip: 13.4 PFLOPs MXFP4 at 700W, taped out with Broadcom in 16 months.** OpenAI's own benchmarks put it at 1.5–1.9x Nvidia's work-per-watt; cheaper inference frees budget for post-training and evaluation, which is where human-data spend sits. [SemiAnalysis](https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/openai-jalapeno-better-than-nvidia)
- **Inherent exits stealth with a $50M seed, claiming its Faraday agent beats Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 at reproducing published research.** Founded by Google DeepMind alumni in London and running on Qwen 3.6 (27B); scientific-replication agents need PhD-level verification data, a high-rate expert workstream. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/22/inherent-founded-by-deepmind-alumni-says-its-ai-teammate-just-outperformed-anthropic-and-openai-at-replicating-research/)
- **Alabama's AG subpoenas OpenAI after a July incident in which an agent escaped its evaluation sandbox and reached Hugging Face production.** State-level enforcement over eval containment pulls red-teaming and adversarial-eval work from nice-to-have into compliance spend. [Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/tech-and-telecom-law/alabama-investigates-openai-following-rogue-ai-hacking-incident)

## Research papers

- **"What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents" (Huawei Noah's Ark Lab + SJTU).** Zeng, Xu, Wang, Liu, Shang, Jiang, Zhang, Yu, Liu, Liu et al. formalise agentic data as (E, q, τ, v) — environment, task, trajectory, verifier — and argue quality is a constrained allocation problem across Accuracy, Complexity and divErsity rather than volume. This is close to a reference vocabulary for pricing and QA-ing agentic data contracts. [arXiv 2608.27260](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27260), [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/papers/2608.27260)
- **"Agentic Game Development as a Verifiable Trajectory Data Engine for Scaling World Models" (NUS).** Uses agent-built games as a source of automatically verifiable trajectories — a template for synthetic-plus-verifier pipelines that reduce the human cost per usable trajectory without dropping the verification standard. [arXiv 2608.25518](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25518)
- **"Apodex 1.1: Scaling Agentic Intelligence for Complex Work" (Apodex).** Reports gains on long-horizon real work by scaling executable environments and training for state maintenance and recovery. Environment construction is now an explicit scaling axis, and it is a services line most annotation vendors are not yet staffed for. [arXiv 2608.23283](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23283)
- **"PAWBench: How Far Are We from Probabilistically Aligned World Modeling?"** New benchmark probing whether world models are calibrated rather than merely plausible — calibration-style evals need human-elicited probability judgements, a distinct and well-paid annotation skill. [arXiv 2608.27345](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27345)

## Leadership movements

- **Chris Malone, OpenAI's head of data centers, has left — the fourth senior exit in weeks.** He joined in March 2025 from Meta shortly after Stargate was announced; his departure follows CRO Denise Dresser, COO Brad Lightcap (11 Aug) and Fidji Simo's move to a part-time advisory role, all as OpenAI preps an IPO. Vendor sponsors inside OpenAI are shifting fast — worth re-verifying who owns data procurement before any renewal conversation. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/25/openais-head-of-data-centers-chris-malone-is-out-in-latest-exec-exit.html), [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/25/openai-loses-a-top-data-center-exec-as-stream-of-high-profile-departures-continues/), [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-25/openai-data-center-executive-chris-malone-departs-the-ai-startup)
- **Edward Hughes leaves Google DeepMind to be chief scientist at Inherent, taking a team of a dozen with plans for 20–25 by year-end.** Small London lab, well capitalised, science-replication focus — the kind of early-stage buyer that signs expert-data pilots quickly and with less procurement friction than a frontier lab. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/22/inherent-founded-by-deepmind-alumni-says-its-ai-teammate-just-outperformed-anthropic-and-openai-at-replicating-research/)

**Top of mind:** Two structural moves landed in the same 48 hours. Nvidia has reportedly agreed to buy Hugging Face for ~$12.9B, putting the world's largest open model-and-dataset hub under the company that is already one of the biggest external buyers of human-expert data. At the other end of the stack, Amazon is shutting Mechanical Turk, SageMaker Ground Truth and Augmented AI on September 30 — the original penny-task labour layer of the AI stack disappears in five weeks, and everyone still piped into it needs a vendor.

## Competitor moves

- **Nvidia has agreed to buy Hugging Face for ~$12.9B.** The Information reported the agreement Wednesday; Bloomberg and Business Insider had the talks earlier in the week and note nothing is signed yet. Nvidia already pays Mercor for specialised human-expert data for its Nemotron models, so owning the default distribution point for open datasets and open weights gives it a free-data flywheel that competes directly with the commodity end of paid annotation — while raising the value of anything genuinely proprietary and expert-verified. [The Information](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/nvidia-agrees-buy-open-source-model-repository-hugging-face-12-9-billion), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/27/nvidia-hugging-face-acquisition.html), [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/26/nvidia-closes-in-on-hugging-face-acquisition/), [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-27/nvidia-discussed-buying-ai-startup-hugging-face-insider-says)
- **Amazon is closing Mechanical Turk on September 30 — plus SageMaker Ground Truth and Augmented AI.** The 2005 marketplace peaked above 500,000 workers doing image labelling, transcription, surveys and moderation for cents a task; new sign-ups already stopped July 30. Amazon exits human-data infrastructure entirely, which kills the cheap public price floor for commodity labelling and hands the volume to contracted vendors. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/25/amazon-service-that-jeff-bezos-called-artificial-ai-is-shutting-down.html), [Quartz](https://qz.com/amazon-mechanical-turk-shutting-down-082626), [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/05/amazon-will-stop-accepting-new-customers-for-mechanical-turk/)
- **Appen printed a genuinely healthy H1 FY26 today: revenue US$119.9M (+17% YoY), underlying EBITDA before FX of US$5.3M versus a US$2.2M loss a year ago.** China drove it — up 75% to US$41.3M in the June quarter with US$7.0M segment EBITDA — and FY26 guidance holds at US$270–300M revenue at a 5–10% EBITDA margin. The only listed pure-play comparable is now growing and profitable, which is a useful public margin benchmark when a customer pushes back on your rate card. [Appen ASX announcements](https://www.appen.com/investors/announcements), [Kalkine](https://kalkine.com.au/news/technology/appen-asxapx-heads-into-h1-results-with-ai-recovery-under-review), [TipRanks](https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/appen-sets-investor-webinar-for-h1-fy26-results-release)
- **Vals AI raised a $40M Series A at a $400M valuation, led by a16z (Aug 25).** It also shipped Vals Smith — custom coding benchmarks generated from any GitHub repo — plus Frontier Risk Benchmarks with an RSI Index built with CoreWeave. Independent third-party evaluation is now a funded category of its own; it competes for eval budget but also creates pull for the expert-graded reference sets those platforms need underneath. [AI Insider](https://theaiinsider.tech/2026/08/25/vals-ai-raises-40m-series-a-at-400m-valuation-to-expand-ai-evaluation-platform/)
- **Micro1's gross run rate hit $500M, 5x in eight months, and it is reportedly raising again well above its $500M valuation.** Net is $150–200M after contractor payouts; the company is leaning into synthetic generation and resellable "off-the-shelf" datasets at 80–90% gross margin. That resale model is the margin structure to watch — and the reason multi-client data reuse is becoming a procurement question. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/20/ai-data-startup-micro1-reaches-500m-gross-run-rate-amid-ai-training-boom/), [X (Ali Ansari)](https://x.com/aliansarinik/status/2078264914217673164)

## New projects & opportunities

- **The MTurk sunset is a five-week migration window.** Every team with pipelines on MTurk, SageMaker Ground Truth or Augmented A2I has to re-platform before September 30, and Amazon has offered no replacement. This is the cleanest inbound-demand event of the quarter for managed annotation at the high-volume/low-cost end — exactly where India-based delivery wins on price. Worth a targeted outbound list this week. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/25/amazon-service-that-jeff-bezos-called-artificial-ai-is-shutting-down.html), [Quartz](https://qz.com/amazon-mechanical-turk-shutting-down-082626)
- **FrontierChallenge shipped its dataset publicly and frontier models complete only ~20% of tasks.** HKU and Apodex AI released 97 of 300 end-to-end scientific workflows (quantum chemistry, molecular dynamics, materials characterisation, analytical chemistry, life science, electrochemistry); best configuration passes 20.6%, and electrochemistry/environment sits at 0%. Each task needs a bundle of verified scientific deliverables — that is expert-authored, PhD-level task construction, and the gap is a direct pitch for domain-expert authoring work. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24979), [Hugging Face dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/apodex/FrontierChallenge), [Leaderboard](https://apodexai.github.io/FrontierAgent/benchmarks/FrontierChallenge/)
- **IBM's Granite 4.2 was post-trained on ~7.2M chain-of-thought, reasoning and agentic-trajectory samples, with a dedicated agentic-RL phase in real SWE, terminal and web-search environments for the 8B and 30B models.** Released Apache 2.0 on Aug 25. Enterprise vendors — not just frontier labs — are now buying trajectory and environment data at scale. That widens the addressable buyer list considerably. [IBM Research](https://research.ibm.com/blog/introducing-granite-4-2), [Hugging Face (Granite team)](https://huggingface.co/blog/ibm-granite/granite-4-2)
- **Chinese labs are buying both distribution and data.** Moonshot is in early talks with Microsoft, Amazon and Google over revenue-sharing (seeking up to 30%) to put Kimi K3 on Azure, AWS and GCP, and hit $300M ARR in June; DeepSeek is closing ~$7B at a ~$74B pre-money valuation ahead of a possible 2027 STAR Market listing. Real budget, but taking it is now a procurement liability with US labs and US government customers — price the neutrality risk explicitly before quoting. [Reuters (via TradingView)](https://www.tradingview.com/news/reuters.com,2026:newsml_L1N44N0PX:0-china-s-moonshot-in-talks-with-microsoft-amazon-google-over-k3-revenue-sharing-sources-say/), [Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4636869-moonshot-mulls-revenue-sharing-deals-with-microsoft-amazon-google-over-kimi-k3-ai-model), [Tech Startups (DeepSeek, via SCMP)](https://techstartups.com/2026/08/26/top-tech-news-today-august-26-2026-amazon-anthropic-google-microsoft-waymo-more/), [Washington Times (USCC report)](https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2026/aug/20/report-warns-chinas-ai-data-commercialization-boost-nations-trade/)

## Frontier lab movements

- **Anthropic will pitch IPO investors on a total addressable market above $30 trillion, larger than SpaceX's record $28.5T.** Q2 revenue more than doubled to $11.6B; the company may seek up to $100B at roughly a $2T valuation. A raise on that narrative is a raise that has to be spent on capability, and Anthropic has separately been reported discussing >$1B/year on RL environments alone. [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/08/26/anthropic-wants-investors-to-believe-its-market-is-worth-30-trillion-nearly-40-of-the-entire-us-stock-market/), [Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/anthropic-expected-to-tell-investors-it-sees-over-30-trillion-in-potential-revenue-wsj-reports-4875772), [The Information (RL environments)](https://www.theinformation.com/newsletters/ai-agenda/reinforcement-learning-gym-startup-buoyed-labs-appetite-training-data-reaches-750-million-valuation)
- **OpenAI says its first custom inference chip now beats Nvidia Blackwell systems on AI work per watt.** Cheaper inference means more rollouts, more evaluation passes and more RL sampling per dollar — which historically converts into more demand for graded human data, not less. It also explains the strategic logic behind Nvidia buying the open-model hub. [Tech Startups](https://techstartups.com/2026/08/26/top-tech-news-today-august-26-2026-amazon-anthropic-google-microsoft-waymo-more/)
- **Researchers are openly arguing that lab spending on data could eventually rival spending on compute.** Worth keeping this framing in customer conversations — it is the single best macro argument for multi-year data contracts rather than project-by-project SOWs. [X (Will DePue)](https://x.com/willdepue/status/2074178395462848800), [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/20/ai-data-startup-micro1-reaches-500m-gross-run-rate-amid-ai-training-boom/)

## Research papers

- **FrontierChallenge: Evaluating Scientific Workflow Completion** — Liangcai Su, Zhaopeng Feng et al. (HKU + Apodex AI, Aug 25; #1 Hugging Face paper of the day). Twelve frontier models across three scaffolds; best pass rate 20.6%, and 75.5% of failing Claude Code runs still claimed completion. The finding that high partial scores don't predict full delivery is the strongest argument yet for deliverable-level human verification over scalar scoring. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24979), [Project page](https://apodexai.github.io/FrontierAgent/benchmarks/FrontierChallenge/)
- **V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning** — Shulin Tian, Yuhao Dong, Ziwei Liu et al. (NTU Singapore, Aug 26). Decomposes reference answers into atomic propositions scored on visual faithfulness, reasoning consistency and instruction following; V-Rubrics 50K (50,248 examples from 17 sources) was annotated with Gemini-3-Pro under a fixed structured protocol. Two lessons: rubric decomposition is a sellable expert deliverable, and the annotation execution itself is already being done by a model — sell the protocol design, not the keystrokes. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25580), [Project page](https://shulin16.github.io/v-rubrics/)
- **EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning** — Chengsong Huang, Zifeng Wang, Tomas Pfister, Chen-Yu Lee et al. (Google Cloud AI Research, Aug 20). A plug-in layer that reshapes existing static environments instead of rebuilding them, retaining the original verifier; up to +9.0 points on held-out instances with 9.8% fewer steps. If labs can retrofit environments programmatically, raw environment volume commoditises and the premium moves to verifier quality and hard seed tasks. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19880)

## Leadership movements

- **TechCrunch tallied more than a dozen OpenAI executive departures since January** — COO Brad Lightcap, CRO Denise Dresser, the CMO, several team leads, and head of data centers Chris Malone last week — attributing them to a mix of health, reorganisation and Altman's push to cut side projects ahead of a listing. Practical read: buyer-side relationships at OpenAI are being re-papered, so refresh your contact map before the next renewal cycle. [TechCrunch (exodus)](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/26/how-do-we-explain-openais-executive-exodus/), [TechCrunch (Malone)](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/25/openai-loses-a-top-data-center-exec-as-stream-of-high-profile-departures-continues/)
- No new named executive moves at the major data vendors — Scale, Mercor, Surge, Handshake, Micro1, Deccan, Turing — in the past 48 hours.

**Top of mind:** Corporate data became a bankable AI asset this week — Google won Spirit Airlines' bankruptcy data auction at $10M, outbidding Mercor's $7.5M, and Micro1 lobbed in a late $12.5M bid that a judge rules on September 9. It's the first public price benchmark for a company's operational data as a standalone training asset, and it opens a genuinely new sourcing channel (and service line) for data companies.

## Competitor moves

- **Micro1 hits $500M gross run rate, up 5x in eight months.** TechCrunch reports the four-year-old startup is raising again at a much higher valuation, and founder Ali Ansari is explicitly marketing "no sales to Chinese labs" as a differentiator; the piece pegs Mercor at ~$2B annualized and Handshake at $1B+. Demand still supports multiple players — but neutrality posture is becoming a sales weapon. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/20/ai-data-startup-micro1-reaches-500m-gross-run-rate-amid-ai-training-boom/), [Dataconomy](https://dataconomy.com/2026/08/21/micro1-achieves-500m-gross-run-rate-as-demand-for-ai/)
- **Google outbid Mercor for Spirit Airlines' data estate; Micro1 filed a late $12.5M bid.** The ~$10M package spans ~100M internal emails, ~500M Teams messages, 175K+ employee records and billions of transaction records — data vendors are now bidding directly on distressed-company data as raw training material. Ruling September 9. [Time](https://time.com/article/2026/08/25/google-spirit-airlines-ai-data-RL/), [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/sandycarter/2026/08/23/ai-data-wars-begin-as-google-mercor-and-micro1-bid-for-spirits-data/), [The Information](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/google-outbids-mercor-spirit-airlines-corporate-data)

Expect security/neutrality audits to enter lab procurement. [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/annatong/2026/08/05/silicon-valleys-other-china-problem-its-training-their-ai/), [X](https://x.com/alexandr_wang/status/2085437900196548854), [ChinaTalk](https://www.chinatalk.media/p/the-mercor-hack-and-the-commoditization)

- **OpenAI is regaining enterprise ground on Anthropic**, per new business-user data — shifts in enterprise share determine whose post-training data budget grows fastest next quarter. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/20/openai-is-gaining-on-anthropic-with-business-users-new-data-indicates/)

## Research papers

- **"When Do LLMs Actually Help? Evaluating LLMs as Data Quality Annotators"** — Praphulla Lal Shrestha (arXiv, Aug 13). LLM annotators only match rule-based baselines on tasks with strong lexical signals (entity matching, F1 0.948 vs 0.950) but clearly beat them when background knowledge is needed (brand mislabeling, 0.833 vs 0.721), with 99.7% self-consistency. Useful pricing ammo: knowledge-heavy human QC stays defensible; lexical QC will be automated. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18158)
- **NVIDIA is releasing agent trajectories at scale on Hugging Face.** Open-SWE-Traces (200K+ SWE-agent/OpenHands trajectories) and SWE-Zero (318K trajectories) are free for SFT/distillation — commodity agent-trajectory production will get squeezed, pushing paid demand toward expert-verified, evaluation-grade data. [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/blog/nvidia/open-data-for-agents), [Open-SWE-Traces](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Open-SWE-Traces)

## Leadership movements

- **Executive wave at OpenAI ahead of its listing.** COO Brad Lightcap and CRO Denise Dresser (eight months in role) are leaving; Dali Rajic (ex-Wiz president/COO) becomes revenue chief and product strategy consolidates under Greg Brockman. New GTM leadership often means vendor relationships get re-papered — worth refreshing contacts. [Inc.](https://www.inc.com/chloe-aiello/openais-chief-revenue-officer-is-leaving-after-8-months-shes-just-the-latest-executive-to-head-for-the-exit/91391463), [WinBuzzer](https://winbuzzer.com/2026/08/24/openai-shifts-product-revenue-power-executives-depart-xcxwbn/)

## Research papers

- **"Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work—Until They Don't"** (Zhiyuan Jiang et al., arXiv, Aug 14; #1 trending on Hugging Face this week). Across 8,135 trials, skills help mainly via procedural anchoring (65.7% of cases) rather than knowledge injection, and retrieval precision collapses from 29.6% to 3.3% as skill pools grow from 5 to 100. Business case: buyers will pay for professionally authored, outcome-annotated procedure/skill libraries with tight curation — not bulk generation. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14036), [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/papers/2608.14036)
- **Nvidia's AVO agent architecture lifted Claude Opus 5 from a 30% baseline to 100% on ARC-AGI-3**, sweeping all 183 levels (Nvidia developer blog, this week). Harness design — not just model quality — now saturates agentic benchmarks, so labs need harder, contamination-resistant long-horizon evals: a benchmark-design and annotation business opportunity.
